nodes.name: Intent Webhook
nodes.notes: The one door (ruled 2026-09-10, door path = the slug of the Rootflow name): POST /webhook/discover-hiring-companies, fired by the Apify task's run webhook. This Insert runs on a scraper payload, not a launch row, so the payload IS the launch row: {signal: <Hub Signals record id>, resource: {{resource}}, tag: <optional>}. `play` is still accepted as the signal key, so an unchanged task keeps firing once its URL is updated. Table is implied (Companies). A bad payload is refused with a Hub row, never a throw.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Parse-Launch.js

nodes.name: Get Play Row
nodes.notes: The Hub Signals row the payload names, by record id alone (ruled 2026-09-10). The old fallback (OR {Signal Type} = 'hiring') kept a retired KB play id working and could only be ambiguous once two clients run the play; an id that resolves to no row is now refused by Parse Play with the fix named. Continues on error, so a dead read is a refusal, not a crash.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Parse-Play.js
@@file:nodes/Client-Vars.js

nodes.name: AT List Tables
nodes.notes: The client base's schema, once, BEFORE any paid call. Companies and the Signals mirror are resolved from it; nothing is created here, the columns are checked by the helper Insert domains to Clayroots.

nodes.name: Find Companies Table

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Find-Companies-Table.js

nodes.notes: Resolves Companies and the Signals mirror off the base's schema. Refuses (never throws) when the base is not ready; Tables OK? routes the refusal to the one Hub row.

nodes.name: Tables OK?
nodes.notes: The refusal gate for the base's schema: false means Find Companies Table named what is missing, and Build Guard Fail Log closes the run before any paid call.

nodes.name: Mirror OK?
nodes.notes: The refusal gate for the Signals mirror row: false means Resolve Mirror Row could not map this Hub signal to exactly one mirror row, and the run closes with that reason before Apify is read.

nodes.name: Get Signal Mirror Row
nodes.notes: Candidate rows in the client base's Signals mirror for this Hub signal, fetched by LOWER(TRIM({Name})) = the signal's name, built upstream by Find Companies Table (2026-09-02: the former match was a synced Record ID column that no client base carries, so every signal died here). The query is permissive on purpose, LOWER and TRIM letting whitespace and case variants through as candidates, because Airtable's = is otherwise exact and case-sensitive (probed live). Resolve Mirror Row then does the strict exact, case-sensitive, client-scoped match and refuses anything but exactly one row, before any paid call. No fields restriction: a fields list naming Client would 422 on a mirror without that column. Companies.Signals links to the mirror row id, never to the Hub row.

nodes.name: Resolve Mirror Row

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Resolve-Mirror-Row.js

nodes.notes: Refuses before any paid call when the mirror row is missing.

nodes.name: Get Scraped Jobs
nodes.notes: The source read: the Apify run's dataset of jobs. Continues on error after three tries (ruled 2026-09-10: a dead provider is a logged skip, never a crash); Filter & Qualify Jobs counts the error item as source_error, and the run closes its Hub row Failed naming Apify with nothing paid for.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Filter-Qualify-Jobs.js

nodes.name: Read Known Signals
nodes.notes: One read by Domain over the qualified domains, before any paid call: which of them already carry THIS signal. Drop Already Signalled drops those.

parameters.jsCode: @@file:nodes/Drop-Already-Signalled.js

nodes.name: DiscoLike BizData
nodes.notes: One call per qualified company, paced 4.5 s apart: DiscoLike allows 5 requests a minute base, 15 on the Team plan, and the ceiling is per key, so every DiscoLike node in the estate holds the same interval (was 2100, about 28 a minute). fullResponse + neverError: Company Facts reads the status and classifies a miss (404) vs an error, which is why this node does not carry retryOnFail. Nothing here throws, so nothing would retry; a 429 lands in the run row as a failure with its reason instead of being silently swallowed.
